openPoints: RESOLVED — TIER 1 (recall never reached the read model). Verified on disk, not from the claim. recall-projection.ts:47 is called from eap-repositories.ts:320 (checkpoint) and :358 (complete), both inside serialTransaction, and RecallWorker.processBatch (recall-worker.ts:111,134) and interruptAndResume (:158,162) always pass the case, so every degradation batch projects. The boundary is drawn where the specs draw it: 004:128 forbids erasing or directly rewriting an admitted record, so `claims` is untouched, and 003:460 defers the destination status of indirect dependents, so only notice.targetClaimIds are written to `recalled`. It is also complete where it matters downstream — eap.ts:269 makes `recalled` terminal instead of falling back to `proposed`, eap.ts:444 refuses promotion of anything not `verified`, eap.ts:568 drops recalled ids from contestable targets, and authorityOf (store.ts:71) reads the `authority` row directly, so graph.impact and the flip gates now see `suspended`. Contestations require a `candidates` row before a target can ever be recalled, so the projection cannot silently miss a target. No further deduction.

RESOLVED — TIER 2 (self-asserted approval freshness). capability-gateway.ts:150 overwrites currentSeq with this.sequences.currentSeq() before authorizeCapability, the constructor hard-fails without an ObservedSequenceSource (:85), and SqliteObservedSequenceSource (eap-repositories.ts:446) reads MAX(seq) from the tenant's horizons. capabilities.ts:153 is now equality, and validateBasedOnSeq bounds by Number.isSafeInteger, so 1e308 no longer reads as fresh. No further deduction.

RESOLVED — TIER 2 (eapRecall interleave) and TIER 3 (JSON.parse cluster). eap.ts:767-790 puts exists(), allocateSequence() and initiateRecallAtomic() in one serialTransaction whose body is synchronous end to end, and ContestationService.initiateRecall (contestation-service.ts:114-154) preceding it is a pure read returning a deterministic `recall-${id}`, so it adds no write outside the unit. Only two JSON.parse calls remain in src/eap (eap-repositories.ts:74 inside parseStored, dependency-query.ts:24 already guarded); StoredStateCorruptionError maps to a typed refusal at eap.ts:903. No further deduction.

TIER 2 — Whole-tenant materialization is unchanged and still on every hot path: persistent-delta.ts:118-119 structuredClones state.graphs and state.claimsCache per admission, incrementalGate spreads the roundtrip index once per candidate, and one recall batch runs three full-table scans in buildRecallExecutionContext (dependency-query.ts:77,89,95) plus a full re-serialization of the case state through write() to SQLite and the JSONL mirror. The new projection sits inside that same per-batch unit and adds a SELECT per suspended cell per batch (recall-projection.ts:82), so a 10k-claim closure driven at batchSize 1 is quadratic in SELECTs before it is quadratic in mirror bytes. This is disclosed and deliberately deferred, which is not the same as absent: for a 100k-claim tenant, what is the event loop doing for the duration of an admission burst, and how large is the JSONL mirror after one large closure processed a claim at a time?

TIER 3 — NEW, and a direct consequence of this change set. Every other writer to the `authority` table pairs the write with an `authority.flipped` event (changeset.ts:384-386), which state.ts:237 lists as ALWAYS_BROADCAST precisely because an ownership change is something every connected session must learn. The projection writes `suspended` through write() alone (recall-projection.ts:85) and emits nothing, while the only TruthOwnershipSuspended events on the tool path (eap.ts:846) come from `progress`, the LAST batch's progress — so with any batchSize smaller than the closure, cells suspended in earlier batches are durably suspended and announced nowhere at all. 003 §Events names the authority view a consumer of that event. If a session that was connected throughout the recall keeps rendering a cell as graph-authoritative, what tells it the graph stopped owning that truth?

TIER 3 — Carried forward, disclosed and unfixed, deducted once as a cluster: eapInitiate is still the one adapter outside serialTransaction while HorizonStore.create does read-then-upsert; persistent-delta.ts:176 still takes COALESCE(MAX(seq),0) for cs_deltas inside a DEFERRED unit; getEvents (eap-repositories.ts:158), getProposalsForParent and the audit list() still materialize whole tenant tables with no pagination, and promotion_events still has no retention policy while the capability audit table has one. Why does the capability audit get a bounded-growth policy and the promotion event log, which grows on the same traffic, not?

TIER 3 — Recall exhaustion is still silent, and the resumption input is now provably dead. eap.ts:827 caps the drive loop at MAX_RECALL_BATCHES and then returns ok:true carrying whatever status settled holds — 'active' for an unfinished case — with no refusal and no distinct field in recallOutcome (eap.ts:882-892) separating it from completion. Meanwhile args.checkpoint is validated at eap.ts:738 and then never read anywhere in the function, so the one parameter a client would use to resume an interrupted recall does nothing. 003:460 lists large-closure batching limits among the boundaries implementation must stop at rather than decide. What does a client do with status 'active' when the payload gives it neither a reason nor a resumption handle it can act on?
architectureTip: The write model and the durable read model now commit together, but the notification channel was left out of that unit: treat the projection as a full read-model port that publishes the same domain event on every state change it applies — one event per suspended cell at the moment it is projected, on the channel the authority view already subscribes to — so that a live session and the authority table cannot disagree either.
